messages:
pagerduty-bot: [P1] Alert: mass routing anomaly detected for policy=capacity-tier-fallback. High error rate and cross-tenant responses observed. Incident created id=INC-20260315-009. Paging on-call.
sre-oncall: Ack. joining. what's the observed customer impact? any immediate mitigation suggested?
eng-oncall: Initial signal: lots of requests from hosted tier are being classified as over-cap and spilled to dedicated pools, but assigned to a shared dedicated pool rather than tenant-dedicated pools. Looks like a policy/templating mismatch in the promoted YAML.
ryan: I pushed the regional promotion of the new fallback template ~10m before the alert. I used the anchor shorthand to reuse rules across regions; could be a scoping bug in the template renderer.
leah: can someone dump the route decision for a sample request? want to confirm which field was wrong (pool_id vs pool_tag)
eng-oncall: grabbing logs now, sample:
```
[2026-03-15T12:01:23Z] route_decision uid=abc123 tenant=tenant-42 incoming_tier=hosted policy=capacity-tier-fallback matched_rule=spill_threshold variant=dyn-v2 assigned_pool=dedicated-shared pool_tag=shared allow_isolation=false fallback_chain=[us-east,us-west,dedicated]
```
eng-oncall: note `allow_isolation=false` — that should be true for any assigned_pool that is dedicated. The template intended to set `pool_tag: tenant-isolated` but rendered `shared` due to anchor scoping.
ryan: ugh, confirmed. local test showed correct render but promotion overwrote the anchor in the region-specific overlay. I'll revert the promotion if we need to.
leah: mitigation plan: 1) set policy into safe_mode (no cross-tier spillover) 2) set a routing ACL to block dedicated-shared pools from receiving hosted traffic 3) notify CS and affected customers. I'll run 1 now.
leah: running: `redwoodctl routing update capacity-tier-fallback --set safe_mode=true --author leah` — applying
opsbot: config apply started: change_id=chg-8812 by leah
opsbot: config apply success: change_id=chg-8812 -> safe_mode=true (propagated to control-plane, 3 regions)
eng-oncall: safe_mode hit. routing decisions now show hosted requests staying in hosted tier or failing closed instead of spilling.
sre-oncall: good. next, put a quick ACL to prevent the dedicated-shared pool from accepting hosted-tagged requests.
leah: `redwoodctl acl add --pool dedicated-shared --deny-from-tag hosted --reason "emergency isolation"`
opsbot: ACL apply success: acl-451 applied
emily-cs: FYI CS update: we've identified 3 customers with confirmed impact (tenant-42, tenant-99, tenant-7). Two reported high latency; tenant-42 reported partial data leakage (different tenant response sample) — mitigation needed fast and we're prepping outreach.
sre-oncall: timeline note: first anomaly 12:00Z, policy promotion 11:50Z, alert triggers 12:02Z. Looks like the promoted overlay introduced an anchor scoping bug.
ryan: I'm reverting the promoted overlay change now and will run a dry render locally to confirm anchors fix.
ryan: revert command: `redwoodctl config revert --change chg-8805 --reason "rollback - policy template anchor bug"`
opsbot: revert queued: chg-8805
opsbot: revert success: chg-8805 reverted (control plane), propagation 2/3 regions
eng-oncall: propagation shows us-west still on old config; forcing rollout there now.
eng-oncall: `redwoodctl rollout force --region us-west --change chg-8805-revert`
opsbot: rollout success us-west
eng-oncall: control plane now consistent across regions. verifying route_decision sample:
```
[2026-03-15T12:08:47Z] route_decision uid=abc124 tenant=tenant-42 policy=capacity-tier-fallback matched_rule=spill_threshold assigned_pool=hosted-pool-12 pool_tag=tenant-isolated allow_isolation=true
```
eng-oncall: looks good. dedicated-shared pool no longer getting hosted traffic. starting validation for 5m window.
sre-oncall: CS, please confirm whether tenant-42 observed any further incorrect responses after 12:09Z.
emily-cs: customer on call says they still see a few errors but much reduced. We're doing a full data integrity check on their last 15 requests.
leah: is there any evidence of persisted data leak in logs (i.e., write actions ending up in wrong tenant index)?
eng-oncall: scanning write logs; no confirmed write-level cross-tenant writes. The issue was routing-level spillover returning cached responses from wrong tenant in some read paths. Cache keys lacked tenant scoping in that dedicated-shared pool — that's a second bug to file.
sre-oncall: okay, immediate tasks: (1) postmortem trigger, (2) ensure cache keys include tenant in dedicated pools, (3) add templating tests for anchor scoping. Who owns (2)?
ryan: I'll take cache-key remediation and add unit tests. I'll open a PR today and set embargo until test passes.
infra-lead: i'll pick up the postmortem and runbook update. assign to infra-oncall and eng-templates.
sre-oncall: severity escalated to SEV2 for cross-tenant exposure risk. owner tags: postmortem=infra-lead, cache-fix=ryan, template-tests=eng-oncall, cs-contact=emily-cs.
emily-cs: outreach update: initial emails sent to tenant-42 and tenant-99, offering detailed logs and mitigation summary. Legal looped in for tenant-42 due to potential partial exposure.
sre-oncall: metric check: token error rate peaked at +18% and p95 latency for hosted traffic increased ~400ms during spill window. We rolled safe_mode at 12:04Z and full revert/protection in place by 12:09Z.
eng-oncall: will schedule a canary deploy of the fixed template with stricter render tests to a single region before full promotion.
leah: creating a short-term guard: add CI lint rule to fail promotions that reuse anchors across overlays unless explicitly namespaced.
opsbot: note: change chg-8812 (safe_mode) will be reverted after postmortem sign-off; mark as temp emergency change.
sre-oncall: handing off monitoring to infra-lead for 08:00-20:00 UTC shift. infra-lead please take runbook and watch for regression for 24h.
infra-lead: taking handoff. summary: routing template anchor scoping bug in promoted overlay caused hosted->dedicated spillover into a shared dedicated pool and cache scoping exposed cross-tenant responses. Emergency mitigations applied: safe_mode, ACL deny, promote revert. Owners assigned. I'll run tabletop tomorrow with eng-templates and cs.
sre-oncall: thanks. closing the active page. keep channel open for updates. please add any follow-ups here.
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT INC-20260315-009 status: resolved (mitigated) at 2026-03-15T12:25:10Z. Follow-up tasks scheduled. :white_check_mark:
emily-cs: adding note: customers requested a timeline + assurance of no persisted leak; we'll provide logs and confirmation once cache revalidation completes.
ryan: PR for cache-key fix opened: https://git.redwood/redwood/PR/31415 — adding tests and linking this incident.
infra-lead: filing postmortem ticket PM-2026-03-15-009 and assigning reviewers. will ping when draft ready.
sre-oncall: good work team, re-assigning to infra-lead for follow-up. :thumbsup:"
